content.intro: This lesson covers Introduction to Smart Pointers. It sits in Module 15, Smart Pointers and Interior Mutability, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Introduction to Smart Pointers matters when you work with type-safe program design. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Introduction to Smart Pointers is one building block of this area: Choose smart pointers and interior-mutability tools that match ownership requirements. Start with the smallest example, identify the inputs and assumptions, and check the edge cases before using the technique in a larger program.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Introduction to Smart Pointers, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Box provides single ownership of heap data, Rc shares ownership in one thread, Arc shares ownership across threads, and interior mutability changes when borrowing is checked.
